extraction.name: Common Corpus
extraction.description: An open, multilingual dataset for LLM pre-training containing 517,033,648 documents and 1,998,647,168,282 tokens. It aggregates six collections: Open Government, Open Culture, Open Science, Open Code, Open Web, and Open Semantic. Content is uncopyrighted or permissively licensed, with document-level provenance, licensing, language, and other metadata.
extraction.license: Document-specific licenses; most content is in the public domain. The ten most common license categories reported are Public Domain, CC-By, MIT, CC-By-SA, Apache-2.0, BSD-3-Clause, Open license, BSD-2-Clause, CC-BY-4.0, and CC0-1.0. Each document's license is provided in its metadata.
extraction.creator: PleIAs
extraction.inLanguage: Multilingual. The ten most represented languages are English, French, German, Spanish, Latin, Italian, Polish, Greek, Portuguese, and Russian. The Wikidata collection covers 300 languages. The dataset also includes programming languages.
extraction.citeAs: Pierre-Carl Langlais, Carlos Rosas Hinostroza, Mattia Nee, Catherine Amett, Pavel Chizhov, Eliot Krzystof Jones, Irène Girard, David Mach, Anastasia Stasenko, and Ivan P. Yamshchikov. Common Corpus: The Largest Collection of Ethical Data for LLM Pre-Training. arXiv:2506.01732v1, 2 June 2025.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Common Corpus aggregates newly collected datasets and pre-existing open datasets. Cultural heritage content was collected through Collections As Data dumps and resource-by-resource retrieval using APIs and other standard retrieval methods. OpenAlex's API supplied scientific-document metadata, licensing information, and original-resource links; records were filtered to CC-By, Public Domain/CC0, and CC-By-SA. Open Code reuses The Stack v1 and v2. Open Web includes Wikimedia rendered-HTML dumps, CC-By YouTube transcripts, and StackExchange data reused from The Pile. Financial and legal documents were collected from public institutions and existing datasets; SEC reports for 2021–2024 were compiled from EDGAR using EDGAR-Crawler. Cultural heritage rights were verified using institutional guarantees and an internal process considering author life, publication dates, and applicable US and EU rules, with Wikidata-based reconciliation.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Software Collection, Web API, User-generated content data
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw sources include digitized books and newspapers, text dumps, PDFs, METS/ALTO XML, financial reports, legal and administrative documents, scientific papers and other research documents, source-code files, Wikimedia rendered HTML, YouTube audio transcripts, StackExchange forums and Q&A, and Wikidata RDF triples. Named sources include SEC/EDGAR, WTO, AMF, TED, GATT, European Parliament and EU repositories, US legal and patent repositories, national libraries and cultural heritage institutions, Internet Archive, Delpher, OpenAlex, arXiv, The Stack v1/v2, Wikipedia, Wikisource, YouTube, StackExchange, and Wikidata.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: The paper describes Common Corpus as an ongoing effort since 2024, with collection continuing at publication on 2 June 2025. Exact collection start and end dates are not provided.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Wikidata items and properties were converted from RDF identifiers into simple natural-language sequences without textual synthesis, with available translations placed in consecutive newline-separated blocks. OCRonos corrects OCR errors, incorrect word splits or merges, and broken text structures; on highly deteriorated content it can perform synthetic rewriting rather than strict correction. Personally identifiable information is replaced with fictitious but realistic values. Documents containing harmful language are either removed or synthetically rewritten without that language.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Segmentext performs text segmentation for broken or unstructured digitized text. OCRoscope, based on cld2, measures unrecognized 7-grams to assess OCR quality and non-character content across at least 80 languages; OCRerrcr provides more accurate but more computationally intensive OCR-error detection. OCRonos corrects digitization errors. Microsoft Presidio, supplemented with custom regular expressions, identifies PII for replacement. Celadon detects toxic content for removal or rewriting. Open Code filtering excludes undesired file extensions and formats, non-permissible licenses, low-quality files using filters described by Lozhkov et al. (2024), and files containing at least 75% digits. Before code filtering, carriage-return/newline sequences are normalized and line lengths recalculated. Cultural and scientific sources are also filtered for public-domain status or permissible licenses.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Each data object contains license, language(s), collection/domain, and other metadata; source URLs and license information are included for the vast majority of the corpus. Language distribution was computed using the fastText language identification model. Celadon identifies harmful content along five dimensions: race and origin-based bias, gender and sexuality-based bias, religious bias, ability bias, and violence and abuse. The EUR-lex source documents were annotated by the Publications Office of the EU with EuroVoc concepts, and the Eurovoc source includes associated EuroVoc labels. No corpus-wide human annotation procedure is described.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: fastText language identification model; Celadon multilingual toxicity classifier; OCRoscope using cld2; OCRerrcr OCR-error detection model; Microsoft Presidio with custom regular-expression patterns for PII detection.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The first Common Corpus collection was published in March 2024, followed by expansions including YouTube Commons in April 2024 and Finance Commons in July 2024. It became a unified corpus in November 2024, and the version described in the paper was released in February 2025. Common Corpus will remain an evolving resource, with HuggingFace archiving past versions for reproducibility. Collection of additional European-language data is ongoing through LLMs4EU, and expansion into African languages such as Swahili, Wolof, and Bambara is planned. No fixed update schedule or deprecation policy is stated.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The paper states that personally identifiable information is identified and replaced with fictitious but realistic values using Presidio and custom regular expressions; phone numbers are explicitly discussed. Cultural heritage rights verification uses author identity, date of death, and US-born status. Language(s) are recorded in document metadata. The paper acknowledges that curation methods cannot achieve 100% accuracy.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Common Corpus is intended to support fully open, auditable, and reproducible LLM development while meeting legal and regulatory requirements, reducing dependence on copyrighted or proprietary training data and associated takedown risks. Its multilingual coverage supports audiences beyond English speakers and contributes to open-science infrastructure. The paper warns that historical texts can reproduce harmful language and describes toxicity filtering and rewriting to mitigate those harms. The project is part of the Current AI initiative to develop open-AI building blocks serving and shaped by the public interest.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Historical public-domain periodicals and monographs may contain language about ethnic groups, women, and violence that does not meet modern ethical standards. The toxicity pipeline addresses race and origin-based, gender and sexuality-based, religious, and ability biases, as well as violence and abuse. Coverage of low-resource languages remains shallow, and nearly 85% of Open Science documents are in English. Filtering and other curation methods are not perfectly accurate.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The corpus does not cover the full range of available open data, and low-resource-language coverage remains shallow. Its approximately two trillion tokens are suitable for pre-training models of limited size; larger models require significantly more data. It contains no instruction-tuning data or specialized-task data and is not directly suitable for task-specific fine-tuning. Curation cannot achieve 100% accuracy. Cultural sources present poor OCR quality, segmentation problems, and sometimes irrecoverable deterioration. OCRonos may synthetically rewrite highly deteriorated text rather than strictly correct it. Users can filter collections using the supplied metadata to avoid potential issues.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Primarily LLM pre-training, either independently or mixed with other open datasets. Document metadata supports filtering by license, language, domain, and creation year. Stated applications include multilingual and historical language models, creative writing, legal and administrative document processing, coding, reasoning, mathematics, structured outputs, vision-language document segmentation, and creation of multimodal datasets, classifiers, synthetic datasets, benchmarks, and ethical fine-tuning datasets. Reported uses include training and evaluation of NVIDIA's NeKo correction model and Anthropic's feature-visualization experiments. The corpus is not directly suitable for instruction-tuning or task-specific fine-tuning.
